back: h(t) = tanh(x(t)·Wxh + h(t−1)·Whh + b). The same weights are used at every time step.
The training signal shrinks as it goes back through many steps, so the network cannot learn long-range effects.
Forget (keep old memory), input (write new idea), output (show memory as hidden state).

front: How is a GRU different from an LSTM?
back: One memory instead of two, and two gates (update, reset). About 25% fewer parameters.

front: Why are RNNs slow to train on long series?
back: Step t needs step t−1, so time steps cannot run in parallel.
